name: fibonacci_breakout_5s
author: adapted from claude-4.6-opus
thesis: After an initial intraday move (>0.5%), price often retraces to a Fibonacci level (38.2%, 50%, or 61.8%) before resuming in the original direction. The breakout occurs when price bounces off a Fib retracement level and breaks above the prior swing high (or below swing low for shorts), confirmed by volume. The Fibonacci extension 161.8% then becomes the target. The edge exists because Fibonacci levels are widely watched self-fulfilling prophecy levels — enough traders place orders at 38.2% and 61.8% to create real supply/demand clusters. However, most traders use Fibonacci on higher timeframes. Applying Fib retracement to intraday swings (1-min bars) is less common and provides faster signals. The inefficiency persists because identifying clean intraday swing highs and lows for Fibonacci anchoring requires real-time swing detection, which most charting platforms do not automate.
mechanism: Fibonacci retracement levels serve as widely-watched reference points where traders cluster their orders. The 38.2% and 61.8% levels attract both stop-losses and limit entries, creating self-fulfilling support/resistance. The concentration of orders at these levels creates measurable price reactions as the order flow interacts with the resting liquidity.

conditions: close pulled back to within 0.1% of fib_382 OR fib_500 OR fib_618
close > fib_level (bouncing off, not breaking through)
close rallied to within 0.1% of (swing_low + 0.382 * range) OR (swing_low + 0.500 * range) OR (swing_low + 0.618 * range)
close < fib_level (rejecting at, not breaking through)

exit.signal_exit: exit if price breaks below the Fibonacci level it bounced off (thesis invalidated)

weaknesses: Fibonacci levels have no fundamental mathematical basis in markets — they are purely self-fulfilling prophecy
Swing detection on 1-min bars is noisy; what constitutes a 'swing' is subjective despite the 5-bar pivot rule
The 161.8% extension target is ambitious and may not be reached intraday; more realistic target may be 100% (prior swing)
prior_art: Fibonacci retracement in trading: widely attributed to R.N. Elliott and popularized by Robert Prechter. Modern application in 'Fibonacci Trading' by Carolyn Boroden. Intraday Fibonacci is discussed by Joe DiNapoli ('DiNapoli Levels'). The specific combination of retracement bounce + extension target is standard Fib methodology.
adaptation_notes: Converted from 1min to 5s bars. Lookback multiplier: 12x. Adaptations: timeframe scaling to 5-second candles; signal conversion from individual stock to NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index; stop/target recalibration for 5-second timeframe. Stop/target calibrated for options point-based exits. Universe narrowed to NIFTY index.
